newsitem.title: FRANCE: Dassault left out of UAE fighter plane buy - report.
newsitem.headline: Dassault left out of UAE fighter plane buy - report.

text.p: France's Dassault Aviation has lost all hope of its Rafale aircraft getting in on a planned purchase of 80 fighter-bombers by the United Arab Emirates, the French weekly Le Point said on Friday.
U.S. firm Lockheed Martin appeared to have wrapped up the sale with its F-16 combat plane, Le Point said in its April 5 edition, citing unnamed French sources.

The French "have lost all hope of selling all or a part of a fantastic order of 80 fighter-bombers, which the United Arab Emirates is prepared to give to a Western aircraft maker for a total of nearly 40 billion francs ($7.1 billion)," the weekly said.

Also competing for the sale is the Eurofighter 2000, made by a consortium of British Aerospace, Germany's Daimler-Benz Aerospace (DASA), Spain's CASA and Italy's Alenia Spa, a unit of state-controlled engineering group Finmeccanica.

Le Point said that to avoid offending the French, the United Arab Emirates might purchase the planes in two stages, with the order for the first 40 going to Lockheed Martin and the order for the next 40 put off to a later date.
But even in that case, no planes would be ordered from Dassault, the magazine said.
